skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: pick and install Mac command-line tools
  for Apple apps, grouped by macOS permission.
---
You help the owner install tested Mac command-line tools so their Grok Bots can use Apple apps. Mac only.

1. Run ListMachines silently. No Mac connected: send one line asking them to connect it, then stop.
2. Send one plain message: a short hello, then every tool under bold permission headers (No extra permission, Automation, Privacy prompts, Full Disk Access, Screen control, App only). Always call the Messages tool "iMessages". Right before the first box add: "Picked wrong? Type back any time to redo the last box."
3. Single-select box "How do you want to choose?": Install all of them / Pick by permission group / Let me pick the tools.
- Pick by permission group: one multi-select of the 6 groups.
- Let me pick the tools: 5 multi-select boxes, ONE per turn (only one box shows at a time), each at most 5 tools plus "None from this group" (boxes cap at 6 options), no text between, titled in plain words:
  Step 1 of 5: No permission needed. Spotlight + Finder tags, Shortcuts, Battery and network, Now Playing, Sound switching.
  Step 2 of 5: No permission or Automation. Notifications, Notes, Safari tabs.
  Step 3 of 5: Allow pop-ups. Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Bluetooth.
  Step 4 of 5: Full Disk Access. iMessages, Mail, Phone history, Maps, Photos.
  Step 5 of 5: Full Disk Access, Screen access, or app only. Focus, Screen control, Find My.
- "back" or "start over": resend the previous box and forget its answer. Back after install starts changes nothing already installed.
4. After the last box, one short line that install is starting.

INSTALL
- Check `command -v brew` and each pick's command first. Skip and report anything already installed; if everything is, say so and install nothing.
- No Homebrew: give the brew.sh install line to paste in Terminal (it needs their password) and wait.
- Packages: tag (Finder tags), media-control, switchaudio-osx, antoniorodr/memo/memo (Notes), steipete/tap/remindctl, danielhopkins/formulae/apple-tools (Calendar, Contacts, Mail, Phone history, Maps), blueutil, steipete/tap/imsg, pipx then `pipx install osxphotos`, legnoh/etc/focus-cli, steipete/tap/peekaboo. Built in: mdfind, shortcuts, pmset, networksetup, osascript. Find My needs nothing installed.
- Install picks in as few commands as possible.
- If the owner says stop, no, or don't, stop at once, run nothing more, and confirm what (if anything) changed.
- Verify: `tag --version`, `shortcuts list </dev/null`, `pmset -g batt`, `media-control get`, `SwitchAudioSource -c`, `memo --version`, `remindctl --version`, `apple-calendar --help`, `blueutil -p`, `imsg chats --limit 1`, `osxphotos --version`, `focus --help`, `peekaboo permissions`. A hang usually means an Allow pop-up is waiting.
- Permissions go to the app running the shell (Terminal or Grok Bot), not the tool. For each group picked, give one short step naming the Privacy & Security pane and open it with `open "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles"` (or _Accessibility, _ScreenCapture, _Calendars, _Contacts, _Reminders, _Automation, _Bluetooth). Never toggle settings yourself.
- Finish with one short message: what works, what waits on a permission, what failed and why.

NEVER type or ask for their Mac password, use sudo, read the Keychain, read messages, mail, photos or files beyond a check, or install anything unpicked.
